To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we provide a generic lower bound on the sample complexity of the active pure exploration problem; (2) this lower bound can be used to derive optimal algorithms for several problems, including best arm, best threshold, best linear, and best Lipschitz bandit problems; and (3) we design Frank-Wolfe based sampling (FWS), an efficient and generic algorithm that solves these optimal algorithms.

(1) we introduce a novel class of pure exploration bandit problems, (2) we provide a general algorithm that solves this class of problems efficiently, and (3) we demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm in several pure exploration tasks.

(i) the lower bounds on the sample complexity of the problem are tight, (ii) they are instrumental in designing efficient active learning algorithms, (iii) Frank-Wolfe is a simple yet efficient tool to solve these lower-bound problems, and (iv) the proposed algorithm is competitive compared to existing algorithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects of pure exploration.
the following question: how to use the lower bound optimization to design efficient algorithms for pure exploration in bandit environments?
the design of efficient active pure exploration algorithms for stochastic bandits, and the study of their performance.

we provide a simple algorithm for a wide range of pure exploration tasks, which is competitive with the state-of-art algorithms, and has a provable sample complexity that matches the information-theoretic lower bound.

the Frank-Wolfe optimization framework is a powerful tool for the design of efficient pure exploration algorithms in bandits.
